column6: Not changed: the claim that Riefenstahl used techniques "borrowed from Hollywood" (incl. telephoto compression) is loosely sourced; not certain enough to edit.
Checked stratigraphy logic: coin minted 50 CE in C gives C and layers above a terminus post quem of 50 CE; older charcoal in B correctly framed as old wood or redeposition.
Old-wood parenthetical said the inner rings came from "a long-lived tree that died long before the tree was felled" (self-contradictory); now says the inner rings formed long before felling.
Bullet 3's correction answers the belief only indirectly (imaginability vs plausibility) but is true.

Bullet 3 belief "Forgeries are deliberate frauds" is true by definition (a forgery is made to deceive); reworded to "Every misattributed document is a deliberate forgery" so the honest-error correction fits. Style: "genuinely old" -> "truly old". Note: Core Idea's "Forgeries—accidental or deliberate" has the same definitional slip; left untouched.
Note: the older Misconceptions section (one bullet, "Thinking that ...; ..." form) does not follow the "- belief. (correction)" format; not in scope, not changed.
Calibration arithmetic checked: slope 4 °C/mm, intercept 10; 0.5 mm -> 12 °C; extrapolation caveat correct.
Expansion D.M. / C. IULIO SECUNDO / VIX. ANN. XL -> Dis Manibus / Gaio Iulio Secundo / vixit annos XL checked (C. = Gaius, dative).
Checked: English legal year began 25 March until 1752, so February 1643 (Old Style year) = February 1644.
Bullet 4 (settlement form gives hypotheses to test) is more cautious than the Explainer's "infer ... before reading a single document"; compatible with Q2's "tentatively".
